displayedInputs.question:
Triangle \(ABC\) is an isosceles triangle with \(\overline{AB}=\overline{BC}.\) Point \(D\) is the midpoint of both \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{AE},\) and \(\overline{CE}\) is \(11\) units long. Triangle \(ABD\) is congruent to triangle \(ECD.\) What is the length of \(\overline{BD}?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Three different one-digit positive integers are placed in the bottom row of cells. Numbers in adjacent cells are added and the sum is placed in the cell above them. In the second row, continue the same process to obtain a number in the top cell. What is the difference between the largest and smallest numbers possible in the top cell?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Barry wrote \(6\) different numbers, one on each side of \(3\) cards, and laid the cards on a table, as shown. The sums of the two numbers on each of the three cards are equal. The three numbers on the hidden sides are prime numbers. What is the average of the hidden prime numbers?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Four circles of radius \(1\) are each tangent to two sides of a square and externally tangent to a circle of radius \(2,\) as shown. What is the area of the square?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

Consider the \(12\)-sided polygon \(ABCDEFGHIJKL,\) as shown. Each of its sides has length \(4,\) and each two consecutive sides form a right angle. Suppose that \(\overline{AG}\) and \(\overline{CH}\) meet at \(M.\) What is the area of quadrilateral \(ABCM?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

A paint brush is swept along both diagonals of a square to produce the symmetric painted area, as shown. Half the area of the square is painted. What is the ratio of the side length of the square to the brush width?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

Circles centered at \(A\) and \(B\) each have radius \(2,\) as shown. Point \(O\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AB},\) and \(OA = 2\sqrt{2}.\) Segments \(OC\) and \(OD\) are tangent to the circles centered at \(A\) and \(B,\) respectively, and \(\overline{EF}\) is a common tangent. What is the area of the shaded region \(ECODF?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

The point \(O\) is the center of the circle circumscribed about \(\triangle ABC,\) with \(\angle BOC = 120^\circ\) and \(\angle AOB = 140^\circ,\) as shown. What is the degree measure of \(\angle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: The given congruence identifies AB with EC. The given equality AB = BC and the midpoint relation then determine BD.
mappings.answerReason: Corresponding sides give AB = EC = 11. Hence BC = 11, and since D is its midpoint, BD = 11/2 = 5.5.

mappings.rationale: The middle digit contributes twice, so the top cell is a + 2b + c. Bounds on the sum of three distinct digits and on the middle digit give attainable maximum and minimum values.
mappings.answerReason: The top equals (a + b + c) + b. Its maximum is 24 + 9 = 33, attained by bottom row (7, 9, 8); its minimum is 6 + 1 = 7, attained by (2, 1, 3). Their difference is 26.

mappings.rationale: Equal card totals couple the hidden primes. Parity and the fact that 2 is the only even prime determine their values, after which their arithmetic mean is calculated.
mappings.answerReason: Let S be the common card total. If S were even, S - 44 and S - 38 would be distinct even primes, which is impossible. Thus S is odd, so S - 59 = 2 and S = 61. The hidden primes are 17, 2, and 23, with average 42/3 = 14.

routes.label: Center distances along a square diagonal

mappings.rationale: Tangency to adjacent square sides places each small center 1 unit from those sides. External circle tangency makes its distance to the large center 3; diagonal geometry or coordinates then determines the square's side and area.
mappings.answerReason: The large center is equidistant from the four corner-circle centers, so it is the square center. For side s, √2(s/2 - 1) = 3, giving s = 2 + 3√2 and s² = 22 + 12√2.

mappings.rationale: The length-4 perpendicular steps give AH = 12 and CG = 8. Similarity or coordinate line intersection locates M, after which splitting ABCM into triangles yields its area.
mappings.answerReason: Since AH is parallel to CG, triangles AHM and GCM are similar, giving AM:MG = 12:8 = 3:2. Thus area(ACM) = (3/5)area(ACG) = (3/5)·16. Adding area(ABC) = 8 gives area(ABCM) = 88/5.

routes.label: Four unpainted triangles and square roots
Strip areas, overlap, and completing the square

mappings.rationale: The painted region is the union of two constant-width diagonal strips. Either calculate the four unpainted isosceles right triangles or add the strip areas and subtract their square overlap, then impose the half-area condition.
mappings.answerReason: For square side s and brush width w, each white triangle has hypotenuse b = s - √2w > 0 and area b²/4. Therefore (s - √2w)² = s²/2. Taking the positive root and rearranging gives s/w = 2/(√2 - 1) = 2√2 + 2.

mappings.rationale: Radii to tangency points are perpendicular to the tangent lines. This produces equal-legged right triangles and 45-degree sectors, allowing the shaded area to be found by subtraction from rectangle ABFE.
mappings.answerReason: AO = 2√2 and AC = 2 give OC = 2, so triangle AOC is right isosceles and sector EAC has angle 45°. Rectangle ABFE has area (4√2)·2 = 8√2. Subtracting two right triangles of area 2 each and two sectors of area π/2 each leaves 8√2 - 4 - π.

mappings.rationale: The desired inscribed angle intercepts the arc AC not containing B. Its central angle is the remainder of the full turn after removing the two marked central angles.
mappings.answerReason: The central angle subtending arc AC opposite B is 360° - 140° - 120° = 100°. The inscribed angle ABC is half of this, so it measures 50°.
